task: send a message that commits you to something, addressed to a specific person (Gmail, Outlook, LinkedIn): draft the email or DM — an outreach, RSVP, request, or reply that creates an obligation — address it to the right recipient, review it as the recipient will read it, send, and verify it shows as sent; complete when the sent state (Sent folder or sent thread) is on screen. Surface pinned: an email client or LinkedIn/professional messaging on web or app. Variants: casual chat with friends, public posts, and mass newsletters do not belong.

tree.label: Send a message that commits you
tree.note: 1 where the session is not already inside the client - most keepers start signed in. 2 picks where the message starts: a blank compose, a mail being answered, a calendar event, or a selected group. 3, 4 and 5 in whatever order the form allows; 4.9 replaces the body on the invite keepers. 6 where the message carries terms beyond its text - buttons, an expiry, a flag, a poll. 7 closes it, or refuses to (NKK1, gBs-, VonO go to 2.6). 8 after every send. 9 where the recipients answer inside the video - votes, a poll grid, an RSVP page, a reply coming back.

children.label: Get into the messaging client
children.note: 1.1 on the phone and browser keepers, 1.2 where the account is not already open, 1.3 whenever a prompt lands, 1.4 in the two keepers who change surface part way.

questions.question: Is the mail app open on your inbox?
questions.why: Seeing the inbox with your recent emails like "Sapang Dalaga MFS" confirms the app is ready for you to start drafting your message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that the agent has successfully accessed the correct email account to initiate the outreach.
questions.check: Is the mailbox view open, showing the inbox message list or an Inbox label?
questions.say_example: Opened <Gmail> to the inbox

questions.question: Which account do you want to send this from?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple account options, so you must choose the correct one to ensure the message comes from the intended sender.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over your sender identity, risking the agent making a commitment on behalf of the wrong account.
questions.check: Does the page show an account chooser listing more than one account? Which email addresses are listed?
questions.say_example: Two accounts here, <[email]> and <[email]>. I'll use <the work one>. OK, or say the other one?

questions.question: Which email address should you use to log in?
questions.why: The Google sign-in screen presents an empty field requiring the specific email address you want to use to access Gmail.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose control over which specific sender identity is used to make the commitment.
questions.check: Is the sign-in page showing an empty email or phone field?
questions.say_example: Signed in as <[email]>

questions.question: Do you want to type the password in yourself?
questions.why: The screen displays the account '[email]', requiring the correct password to authenticate and proceed to the email client.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to keep their password private and manually control the authentication process.
questions.check: Is a password field shown, with a label like 'Enter your password' or 'Password'?
questions.say_example: It's asking for your password. I won't type that. The field is yours. Say done when you're in.

questions.question: Does your calendar already have something at the time you're about to commit to?
questions.why: The screen shows a navigation bar in the bottom left with a Calendar icon, which you need to click to view your schedule before making a commitment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you trust the agent to accurately interpret your calendar and avoid double-booking you.
questions.check: On the calendar for <date>, is any event shown overlapping <time>? What is its title?
questions.say_example: You're about to say <Tuesday at 2>. Your calendar already has <Lab meeting> then. Pick a different time, or say send anyway?

children.label: Start the message
children.note: one of 2.1, 2.3, 2.4, 2.5 or 2.7 opens the compose surface - 2.2 first where the message answers a mail. 2.6 whenever a started draft is thrown away: before the real compose in VonO, and instead of a send in NKK1 and gBs-. 2.7 on a professional network, where the message starts from the person's profile rather than from a compose button.

questions.question: Is this a new message, a reply, or a forward? Is that what you asked for?
questions.why: Locating the red pencil icon is required to open the compose screen and begin drafting the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to start a brand new email or reply to an existing thread to make your commitment.
questions.check: Does the compose header show a subject starting with Re: or Fwd: with a quoted thread below it, or an empty subject with no quoted thread?
questions.say_example: You asked me to reply on <name>'s thread. This is a brand new message. It wouldn't show up in the thread. I'm switching to a reply.

questions.question: Which email should you open?
questions.why: The inbox shows a welcome email from the Google Community Team, presenting a choice of which message to interact with.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the ability to decide which specific email to open and potentially reply to.
questions.check: Does the inbox list more than one message from <sender>, or more than one matching <subject>? What are their dates and subjects?
questions.say_example: Two messages from <name>. One from <Monday> about <the budget>, one from <today> about <the deadline>. Which one? Say Monday or today.

questions.question: Is this message from a no-reply address that nobody reads?
questions.why: The screen displays an automated welcome email from the Google Community Team, which informs the decision of whether this is an appropriate recipient for a commitment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that their commitment is being sent to a valid, human recipient rather than an automated mailing list.
questions.check: Is the sender address of the open message a noreply or no-reply address, or does the message say not to reply?
questions.say_example: This one came from <noreply@…>. Nobody reads replies there. Want me to find <name>'s real address instead?

questions.question: Does the message ask for more than one thing? Which are you answering?
questions.why: The screen showed a detailed email paragraph, and highlighting a specific sentence clarifies exactly which point the reply will address.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to steer the conversation by selectively focusing on a specific detail or offer from the original message.
questions.check: Does the open message contain more than one request or question? Quote each.
questions.say_example: <name> asks two things. When you can deliver, and whether you'll join Friday. Answer both, or just one?

questions.question: Are there older messages folded away in this thread?
questions.why: The screen shows older messages are collapsed, which hides the full history of the conversation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the agent considers the entire conversation history before drafting a reply.
questions.check: Does the thread show collapsed earlier messages, such as a count of older messages or an ellipsis?
questions.say_example: Opened <3> older messages folded away in the thread

questions.question: Should you reply to just the sender or reply all to include everyone on the thread?
questions.why: The screen displays 'Reply', 'Reply all', and 'Forward' buttons, and selecting the right one determines who is kept in the loop regarding your commitment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means losing the personal judgment of whether all participants in the thread need to be aware of your response.
questions.check: Does the original message list more than one address in To or Cc besides yours? Which ones?
questions.say_example: <name> also copied <[name]> and <[name]>. Reply just to <name>, or reply all?

questions.question: Is the new event on the date you want, or just the day the calendar opened on?
questions.why: The screen displays the daily schedule for April 1, 2019, and clicking the '+ New' button in the toolbar is required to open the event creation form.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to visually confirm that the calendar is set to the correct date before starting the draft.
questions.check: What date does the new event's date field show?
questions.say_example: The event landed on <April 1>. That's just the day the calendar opened on. You wanted <April 8>. Fixing it.

questions.question: Do you want to create a calendar event instead of a standard email?
questions.why: The 'New mail' button includes a dropdown menu with an 'Event' option, letting you initiate an invite directly from the inbox.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose whether a formal calendar invite or a standard email is the best way to frame your commitment.
questions.check: Does the compose menu show an Event option, and is the event form open?
questions.say_example: Started a calendar invite instead of an email, as asked

questions.question: Do you want to throw this draft away?
questions.why: The screen showed a dialog box asking to confirm whether to abandon the modified draft.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The person loses the time and effort spent writing the message if the agent mistakenly discards the draft.
questions.check: Is a dialog shown asking to discard or abandon the draft? What does the draft contain?
questions.say_example: It's asking whether to throw the draft away. There's <a paragraph> written. Throw it away, or keep it?

questions.question: Does messaging this person use a paid InMail credit, or does their profile offer a free way to reach them?
questions.why: The gold 'in' logo indicates a Premium member, which means they might have the open profile feature enabled for free messaging.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to save your paid InMail credits by strategically targeting users with open profiles.
questions.check: Does the page say messaging this person uses an InMail credit, or show Open profile or free message? How many credits remain? Does Contact info list an email?
questions.say_example: Messaging <name> uses one InMail credit. You have <4> left. Their profile also lists an email, <name@…>, which is free. InMail, or email?

children.label: Set the recipients
children.note: 3.1 on a blank message; 3.2 where the tutorial bothers with copies; 3.3 where an address book exists. 3.4 before 3.1 in kvML and on every mobile compose whose From line is on screen. 3.5 replaces 3.1 on the group keepers. 3.6 replaces it on the invite keepers. 3.7 wherever the platform asks what the recipients may see.

questions.question: Who are you sending this email to?
questions.why: The screen showed a dropdown of suggested contacts after typing 'ia' in the 'To' field, requiring a choice of the correct recipient.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the ability to personally select the exact recipient from their contacts or suggestions.
questions.check: What name and address does the To chip show, and does it match the recipient named in the ask?
questions.say_example: The To field picked <[email]>. You said <[name] at work>. Changing it to <[email]>.

questions.question: Which of their addresses do you want to use?
questions.why: The dropdown showed both a Gmail and a Hotmail address for the same person, requiring you to know which one is their active or preferred account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to apply your personal knowledge of the recipient's correct contact information when multiple options appear.
questions.check: Does the autocomplete list two or more addresses for the same name? Which addresses?
questions.say_example: <name> has two addresses here, a Gmail and a Hotmail. Which one? Say Gmail or Hotmail.

questions.question: Is there more than one person with this name in the suggestions?
questions.why: Autocomplete often suggests multiple contacts with identical or similar names, relying on visual cues like avatars or secondary domain text to differentiate them.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks sending a binding commitment to the wrong person because the agent selected a matching name without verifying the visual context.
questions.check: Does the autocomplete list more than one person with the same name? What distinguishes them: the address domain, the avatar, the title?
questions.say_example: There are two people called <[name]> here. One at <stanford.edu>, one at <gmail.com>. Which one? Say Berkeley or Gmail.

questions.question: Does it say this person is out of office?
questions.why: The platform often surfaces the recipient's away status as soon as their address is added, which might require you to change the deadline of your commitment or CC a secondary contact.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate situational awareness that the recipient is unavailable, risking a time-sensitive commitment sitting unread.
questions.check: Does the compose window show an away or out-of-office banner for <recipient>? What dates does it give?
questions.say_example: <name> is out until <Sep 12>. Your message asks for an answer by <Friday>. Send it anyway, or copy <someone else>?

questions.question: Is anyone on this outside your company?
questions.why: Corporate email clients flag external recipients with a banner or tooltip to prevent accidental sharing of sensitive commitments or data.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the security check that prevents them from accidentally making a commitment to an external or unauthorized party.
questions.check: Does the page show an external or outside-your-organization banner or tag on a recipient? Which address?
questions.say_example: <address> is outside <your company>. The message has <the contract terms> in it. Still send?

questions.question: Do the Cc and Bcc fields hold exactly the people you asked to copy?
questions.why: The 'Cc' button next to the 'To' field allows you to include additional stakeholders who need visibility into the commitment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide which specific colleagues or stakeholders need to be kept in the loop based on nuanced professional context.
questions.check: What addresses are in Cc and Bcc, and do they match the copy recipients in the ask?
questions.say_example: You asked to copy <[name]>. Cc is empty. Adding her.

questions.question: Is every attendee you named found in the address book, or does one need typing by hand?
questions.why: The dialog box provides a list of saved contacts to select from, but also includes a text box where unlisted addresses must be entered manually.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might only select from the visible list of contacts and fail to manually include necessary external participants.
questions.check: Does the address book search return no match for <name>?
questions.say_example: <name> isn't in your address book. I'll type <address> in by hand. Is that the right address?

questions.question: Which email address should you send from?
questions.why: The 'From' field on the compose screen offered multiple sender addresses, which determines the identity attached to this commitment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to select the most appropriate sender identity for this specific recipient and obligation.
questions.check: What address does the From field show, and does it match the account you signed in with or the one the ask named?
questions.say_example: This would go out from <alias@…>, not your <main address>. Switching it.

children.label: Build the recipient set
children.note: 3.5.1 then 3.5.2 then 3.5.3 in I57x - the set is a tag. 3.5.1 then 3.5.2 in zZ3x - the set is a saved pipeline. 3.5.4 in both, once per page. 3.5.5 after 3.5.4 - the count changes and nothing on screen says why.

questions.question: Is there more than one profile with this name?
questions.why: The dropdown displayed multiple profiles for 'John Smith' alongside generic search terms, meaning a full search might be needed to accurately identify the correct recipient.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to review the full search results and ensure the agent selects the exact right person to message.
questions.check: Do the search results list more than one profile with the name <name>? What headline and location does each show?
questions.say_example: Three people called <John Smith>. One's a <designer in Amsterdam>, one's in <telecom in Rotterdam>. Which one? Say designer or telecom.

questions.question: Is the person you want on the first page of results, or on a later page?
questions.why: The specific person you needed to contact did not appear on the first page of the search results.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manually scan the results and visually identify the correct recipient's profile among similar names.
questions.check: Does page 1 of the results list <name>? Is there a next page or pagination control?
questions.say_example: <name> isn't on the first page. There are <4> more. Checking them before I give up.

questions.question: Do the search filters match what you asked for?
questions.why: The screen showed specific filters like 'Solution Designer', 'Netherlands', and 'Telecommunications' being applied to find the right person to message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to fine-tune search criteria based on their nuanced understanding of the exact profile they want to reach.
questions.check: Which filter chips are shown as applied, and do they match the ask?
questions.say_example: The search is filtered to <Netherlands> and <telecom>. You said <Belgium>. Changing it.

questions.question: Do you want a new project made for this outreach?
questions.why: The screen shows a '+ Create new project' option under the Projects dropdown, which dictates how this new task will be organized.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to organize this new commitment under a brand new project or an existing one.
questions.check: Is the Create new project option shown, and was creating a project part of the ask?
questions.say_example: Made a project called <Q4 designers>, as asked

questions.question: How should you name and describe the new project?
questions.why: The 'Create project' modal includes fields for 'Name' and 'Description' that determine how the project is identified and shared with colleagues.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses their personal naming convention that includes key details like location, duration, and owner for team visibility.
questions.check: What do the Name and Description fields hold?
questions.say_example: Named the project <Q4 designers>

questions.question: Which tags should you apply to this connection?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Tag' dropdown menu with custom options like 'Queen's' and 'classmates', requiring a choice on how to categorize this contact.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent lacks the personal context of your real-world relationships to accurately assign custom organizational tags to your connections.
questions.check: Which tag is shown on the connection?
questions.say_example: Tagged <name> as <classmates>

questions.question: Which tag do you want to filter by?
questions.why: The filter menu contains multiple custom tags like 'Queen's' and 'colleagues', so selecting the correct one ensures you isolate the intended audience.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally decide which specific professional or social circle to target for this commitment.
questions.check: Which tag chip is shown as the active filter?
questions.say_example: The list is filtered to <colleagues>. You said <classmates>. Switching.

questions.question: Do you want to message everyone on the page, or only the ones the page says are likely to respond?
questions.why: The screen displays valuable filtering signals like '13 are more likely to respond' and '9 open to new opportunities' that are ignored when bulk-selecting the entire page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the strategic advantage of personalized targeting, resulting in outreach being sent to potentially unqualified or unresponsive individuals.
questions.check: Is a select-all control about to be used, and does the page show counts like 'N more likely to respond' or 'N open to opportunities'? What are the counts?
questions.say_example: Select all would message all <25>. The page says <13> are likely to respond. All <25>, or just those <13>?

questions.question: Are the candidates on the later pages selected too, or only the first page?
questions.why: The narrator explains that you must scroll down and use the pagination controls to select the next batch of candidates, even though the action itself is not shown on screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the assurance that the agent knows how to navigate multiple pages to include all intended recipients in the outreach.
questions.check: How many candidates does the page say are selected, and how many are in the filtered list in total?
questions.say_example: You said everyone in the list. That's <53>. Only <25> are selected, the first page. Selecting the rest.

questions.question: Did everyone you picked land in the pipeline?
questions.why: The screen displayed a pipeline count of 50 despite showing 53 total candidates, which matters because it indicates that some candidates opted out of receiving emails.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that specific candidates were automatically excluded from the outreach message due to their communication preferences.
questions.check: Does the page show a pipeline or added count lower than the number selected? Does it say why, such as opted out?
questions.say_example: You picked <53>. <50> made it in. The page says <3> opted out of email. They won't get this.

questions.question: Who should you invite to this event?
questions.why: The 'Add guests' field and dropdown allow you to select the specific email address to receive the calendar invite.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over who receives the event invitation and what permissions they are granted.
questions.check: What names are in the guest list, and do they match the people named in the ask?
questions.say_example: The guest list has <[name]> but not <[name]>. Adding him.

questions.question: Is the event visibility set to Public, so anyone with your calendar can read the details?
questions.why: The visibility dropdown offers options like Public and Private, which determines whether others can read the meeting details or just see a busy block on your calendar.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might leave the visibility on the default setting, potentially exposing sensitive meeting details to anyone who has access to view your calendar.
questions.check: What does the visibility field show: Default, Public, or Private?
questions.say_example: This event is set to Public. Anyone who can see your calendar could read <the details>. Switch to private?

questions.question: Can guests change this event, including the time?
questions.why: The screen showed checkboxes for guest permissions, which determines how much control the attendees will have over the calendar event.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether guests can alter the event details, invite additional people, or view the full attendee list.
questions.check: Which guest permission boxes are checked: modify event, invite others, see guest list?
questions.say_example: Guests can change this event. <name> could move the time. Want that off?

questions.question: Do you want to hide the recipients from each other so the message is sent privately?
questions.why: The screen shows a checkbox below the send button that dictates whether the message is sent as a visible group or as private individual messages.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over their contacts' privacy and the social dynamics of sending a group versus individual message.
questions.check: Is the message addressed to more than one recipient, and is there a checkbox to send to each recipient individually or hide recipients? Is it checked?
questions.say_example: This goes to <6> people at once. They'd all see each other's names. Send it to each one privately instead?

children.label: Write the message
children.note: 4.1 and 4.2 on every keeper that sends text; 4.3 where the mail is a job application; 4.4 and 4.5 on the reply keepers; 4.6 to 4.8 where the body is designed rather than typed. 4.9 replaces 4.2 on the invite keepers, and inside it 4.9.8 replaces 4.9.2 and 4.9.3 when the times are polled instead of set. 4.10 replaces 4.1 and 4.2 on a connection request, where the whole message is one optional note.

questions.question: What should the subject line be?
questions.why: The compose screen provides a subject field to give the recipient immediate context about the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over how the email is introduced and framed for the recipient.
questions.check: What does the subject field hold?
questions.say_example: Set the subject to <Friday delivery>

questions.question: Is the subject empty, or does it say something different from what's attached or written?
questions.why: The screen showed an empty subject field at 2:26, making it important to verify that the final subject line matches any attached files before sending.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to catch discrepancies between the email's subject and its attachments, which could confuse the recipient.
questions.check: Is the subject field empty, or does it name something different from the attachment name or the body?
questions.say_example: The subject is empty. I'm putting <Pictures> in so <name> knows what this is.

questions.question: What should you write in the body of the email?
questions.why: The compose screen is ready for the main text, which must clearly convey your intended message and tone.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over the exact phrasing, language, and personal tone of the message.
questions.check: What does the body say? Quote the sentence that makes the commitment.
questions.say_example: Here's what I wrote. You'll have the report to <name> by <Friday>. Say change if that's not it.

questions.question: Does the message tell people there are voting buttons?
questions.why: Voting buttons can be subtle, so explicitly mentioning them in the subject and body ensures they are not missed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the nuanced communication strategy of explicitly directing recipients to use specific UI features.
questions.check: Are voting buttons enabled, and does the subject or body mention them?
questions.say_example: Voting buttons are on, but the message doesn't say so. Some mail apps hide them. Adding a line at the top that says to vote.

questions.question: Is 'send a copy to me' checked in the Email guests dialog?
questions.why: The 'Email guests' dialog contains an empty message field for your note and a default-checked option to send a copy to yourself.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to dictate the exact wording of the message and decide whether you need a personal copy for your records.
questions.check: Is the send-me-a-copy box checked?
questions.say_example: Left the send-me-a-copy box checked

questions.question: Is the new template set to be shared with your team, or kept private?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'New Template' dialog with options to share the template with team members or keep it private, along with fields for the template name and subject.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over whether their custom template is shared with their team or kept private.
questions.check: Which sharing option is selected in the New Template dialog?
questions.say_example: Saved the template as private, just for you

questions.question: Is there already a thread with this person to reply in?
questions.why: The messaging sidebar displays past threads like the one with [name], allowing you to reference previous interactions for tone and context while drafting.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally select the most relevant past conversation to use as a benchmark for your new message.
questions.check: Does the messaging sidebar list an existing thread with <recipient>? What is its date?
questions.say_example: You already have a thread with <name> from <March>. I'll reply there instead of starting a new one. OK?

questions.question: Is your reply above the line the sender marked, not on it or below it?
questions.why: The compose box displays a clear instruction to reply above a specific line, indicating that text typed on or below it may not be processed correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over the exact placement of their text, risking that their commitment gets buried or stripped out by the recipient's email system.
questions.check: Expand any collapsed quote in the compose box. Is there a marker like 'reply above this line'? Is the typed text above it? Is a full editor open, rather than a quick reply chip?
questions.say_example: The reply landed below the line that says reply above it. <name>'s system would drop it. Moving it up.

questions.question: Is there leftover text in the draft, like an old signature?
questions.why: The user attempted to select all content using a keyboard shortcut, but only the text portion of the signature was highlighted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the ability to ensure unwanted auto-populated content is completely removed before drafting their message.
questions.check: Does the draft body contain leftover text besides the new message, such as an old signature or 'Sent from …'?
questions.say_example: There's leftover text under your message, <'Sent from Yahoo Mail for iPhone'>. Taking it out.

questions.question: Is someone who wasn't on the earlier thread about to get the whole quoted history?
questions.why: When forwarding a message or adding new recipients to a thread, the entire previous conversation is included by default, which might expose private discussions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the human judgment to review the hidden thread history and delete sensitive parts before exposing them to new participants.
questions.check: Is any address in To or Cc absent from every earlier message in the quoted thread, and is the quoted thread included in the draft?
questions.say_example: <name> wasn't on this thread before. The whole history goes with it, including <Monday's numbers>. Trim it, or send it all?

questions.question: Which signature should you insert into the email?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Signature' dropdown with options like 'Burntolearn', requiring a choice of which sign-off best fits the context of your message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to select the most appropriate professional branding or contact information for this specific recipient.
questions.check: Which signature is shown at the bottom of the draft?
questions.say_example: Signed off with your <work> signature

questions.question: Which saved template should this bulk message use?
questions.why: The screen shows an empty message modal and a template dropdown, requiring a choice to correctly populate the outreach text.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the assurance that the exact right template is chosen for this specific professional outreach.
questions.check: Does the template dropdown list more than one template, and did the ask name one? What are they called?
questions.say_example: Three templates here, <Intro>, <Follow up>, <Event>. Which one? Or I can write it fresh.

children.label: Fill in the event details
children.note: 4.9.1 then 4.9.2 then 4.9.3, or 4.9.8 in place of 4.9.2 and 4.9.3 when the times are put to a vote. 4.9.4 to 4.9.7 where the form shows them - ixyD accepts a recurrence the form derived from the date, and 3qL6 opens every dropdown and changes none.

questions.question: What should you title the event?
questions.why: The screen prompts for an event title, which serves as the primary subject or identifier the recipient will see.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose exactly how their name or the commitment is presented to the recipient.
questions.check: What does the event title field hold?
questions.say_example: Titled the event <Design review>

questions.question: Is this all day, or does it have a start and end time?
questions.why: Unchecking the 'All day' box revealed specific time fields, allowing the user to define exact boundaries for the commitment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to dictate their exact availability, risking an agent committing them to an all-day obligation or an incorrect time slot.
questions.check: Is the All day box checked, and did the ask give a clock time?
questions.say_example: It's set to all day. You said <2 pm>. Unchecking it and putting the time in.

questions.question: Does the scheduling grid show an attendee busy at the time you're proposing?
questions.why: The scheduling grid displays free timeslots without a person icon, which is essential for proposing a time that works for the recipient.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally select a mutually convenient time based on the visual cues in the scheduling grid.
questions.check: On the scheduling grid, is <attendee> marked busy or unavailable at <time>? Which slots are free for everyone?
questions.say_example: The grid shows <name> is busy at <2>. Everyone's free at <3>. Move it?

questions.question: What should you set as the event's end time?
questions.why: The default 30-minute duration needed to be manually adjusted to 20 minutes to accurately reflect the actual length of the lesson.

questions.question: What goes in the description?

questions.question: Does the sent forward include the original message under your note?
questions.why: The screen showed a collapsed forwarded message with a '> Show original message' link, requiring you to expand it to verify the full text.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the assurance that the forwarded content was correctly included and formatted in the final sent message.
questions.check: With the original expanded in the sent copy, is the forwarded message text present?
questions.say_example: The forward went out with nothing under your note. <name>'s original didn't come along. Send it again with the text?

questions.question: Has a bounce come back saying the message didn't get through?
questions.why: The top email in the inbox showed an 'Address not found' snippet, meaning the message did not reach the recipient.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user falsely believes their commitment was communicated, leaving the recipient unaware.
questions.check: Is there a new message in the inbox with Address not found, Delivery failed, or a bounce for <recipient>?
questions.say_example: A bounce came back. <name>'s address wasn't found, so it never got there. Check the address?

questions.question: Did an auto-reply come back saying they're away?
questions.why: An immediate automated response indicates the recipient is unavailable, meaning the time-sensitive commitment may not be seen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that their message wasn't actually received by a human, failing to redirect the commitment to an available contact.
questions.check: Did an auto-reply or out-of-office message arrive from <recipient>? What return date does it give?
questions.say_example: <name>'s auto reply says they're away until <Sep 12>. Your message wanted an answer by <Friday>. Send it to <someone else> too?

children.label: Handle the responses
children.note: 9.1 for the sender's own vote, 9.2 for the others; then 9.3 and 9.4 as the tally comes in. 9.5 when the poll decides a meeting. 9.6 on the invite link. 9.7 on the recruiting side. 9.8 where the corpus fails and shows no repair. 9.9 last, in one keeper.

questions.question: Which option is selected in your own vote, and is it sending now?
questions.why: The screen displays a voting dropdown with cuisine options and a dialog asking whether to send the response immediately or edit it first.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to select their preferred choice and decide whether to add additional context before the vote is sent.
questions.check: Which option is selected in the vote dropdown, and is it asking to send now or edit first?
questions.say_example: Voted <Thai> on your own poll

questions.question: What's the tally, and who hasn't voted?
questions.why: The Message Tracking window displayed the reply totals and individual responses, which dictates the outcome you are committing to in the message.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally review the voting breakdown and ensure the correct choice is made based on the group's preferences.
questions.check: What totals does the tracking window show per option, and which recipients have no response?
questions.say_example: Votes are in. <3> for Thai, <1> for Italian. <Bill> hasn't voted.

questions.question: Book the meeting on the votes so far, or wait for everyone?
questions.why: The screen shows that required attendees like Bill Lumbergh haven't responded yet, and the preferred 2:30 PM slot already has one 'No' vote.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the nuanced human judgment of weighing strong preferences against outright rejections and knowing when to wait for crucial stakeholders before committing.
questions.check: Does the poll page show required attendees with no response, or a No on the slot about to be chosen?
questions.say_example: <Bill> hasn't voted, and <2:30> already has one no. Book it anyway, or wait for him?

questions.question: Does the event page match the invite's date and time?
questions.why: Checking the event landing page ensures the recipient will see the correct date, time, and functional Yes, No, or Maybe buttons.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the peace of mind that comes from manually verifying the recipient's exact view of the event details and RSVP options.
questions.check: Does the event page show the date, time and Yes, No, Maybe buttons matching the invite?
questions.say_example: The event page says <3 pm>. The invite says <2>. Everyone invited would see the change. Fix the event to <2>?

questions.question: What should go in the candidate's notes?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Note' icon and existing notes, indicating this is the designated place to maintain context about the candidate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the assurance that nuanced insights, such as salary expectations or contact preferences, are captured for future interactions.
questions.check: What text is in the candidate's notes?
questions.say_example: Noted <messaged about the design role> on <name>'s profile

questions.question: Has someone on your team already messaged this person?
questions.why: The Recruiting Activity feed displays notes, views, and message counts from colleagues, which helps you avoid sending redundant or conflicting outreach.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness of your team's prior relationship with the recipient, which could lead to an uncoordinated or embarrassing message.
questions.check: Does the activity feed show a message or note from a colleague to this candidate? Who and when?
questions.say_example: <[name]> already messaged <name> <two weeks ago>. Yours might double up. Still send?

questions.question: What status should the candidate get now that you've messaged them?
questions.why: The screen shows a "Change status" dropdown with options like "Contacted" and "Screened" to track the candidate's progress.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to define their own workflow rules for categorizing candidates in the pipeline.
questions.check: What does the Change status dropdown show?
questions.say_example: Marked <name> as contacted

questions.question: What does the send error say?
questions.why: The screen displays an error state in the chat window that must be cleared using the 'X' button so you can return to the main interface and resolve the issue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally read the error details and understand what caused the failure before the alert is dismissed.
questions.check: Is an error shown after send? Quote its text.
questions.say_example: It didn't send. The error says <'Message not delivered'>. I'm leaving it on screen. Try again, or a different way?
